name: Electrochemical Dissolution Sprayer EDS-2 'Lacquer'
description:
The EDS-2 generates a fine aerosol of electrochemically activated solvent compounds by passing a base liquid reagent through a high-voltage ionization grid immediately before ejection. The ionization process transforms the reagent from an inert transport medium into a highly reactive dissolution agent that aggressively attacks both organic polymers and biological lipid membranes. The spray itself is nearly invisible — a faint iridescent shimmer in direct light — making it exceptionally difficult to detect in dimly lit environments until contact is made.

What makes the EDS-2 distinctively dangerous is the selectivity of its ionization profile. By adjusting the voltage gradient on the ionization grid via a thumb dial on the grip, operators can tune the reagent's reactivity toward organic tissue, synthetic materials, or a balanced blend of both. At maximum organic setting, it strips exposed skin and mucous membranes within seconds; at maximum synthetic setting, it dissolves polymer armor coatings, adhesives, and certain cybernetic housing materials. The mixed setting is considered the most tactically versatile but produces a caustic byproduct fog that requires the operator to wear sealed respiratory protection.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the EDS-2 ostensibly as an industrial decontamination tool for hazardous polymer environments, and it remains technically legal as such in several Meridian 88 jurisdictions — a loophole that has made it a favorite of operators who need plausible deniability on weapon checks. The weapon is recognizable by its wide conical nozzle, dual reagent tanks (one base liquid, one ionization catalyst), and the faint electrical crackling audible during active discharge.
legality: Restricted (licensed industrial use only; unlicensed carry Prohibited)
specifications:
effective range: 2–12 meters (aerosol cone)
dispersal angle: 15-degree cone
reagent capacity: Base tank: 400ml / Catalyst tank: 200ml
ionization voltage: 8,000–14,000V adjustable
tuning modes: Organic (O-mode), Synthetic (S-mode), Mixed (M-mode)
continuous discharge duration: Approximately 22 seconds per full tank
weight: 4.2 kg loaded
operator protection required: Sealed respiratory mask recommended in M-mode
dimensions: 44cm overall, 18cm nozzle assembly
tactical_use: Operators use the EDS-2 to strip defensive advantages from targets before engagement — dissolving armor polymer coatings, removing adhesive traps, or degrading cybernetic housing to expose internal components. In close-quarters situations, the organic setting is used as a disabling tool: even brief facial exposure causes involuntary eye closure and severe respiratory distress, forcing targets out of cover. Industrial sabotage specialists use the synthetic setting to destroy equipment without leaving ballistic evidence. The aerosol's near-invisibility makes it effective as a trap layer in ventilation systems.
cultural_context: In Meridian 88's corporate espionage circles, being 'lacquered' has become slang for having your defenses methodically stripped before a hostile move — professional, financial, or physical. The EDS-2's industrial licensing loophole is an open secret, and Zheng-Dao Bioelectric has never publicly acknowledged the weapon applications of the device, maintaining a posture of corporate innocence while quietly supplying the gray market. Operators who carry it are often perceived as precise and methodical rather than aggressive — the weapon suggests patience.
known_users: Corporate sabotage specialists and competitive intelligence operatives
'Varnish' — an anonymous fixer known for leaving dissolved equipment as a calling card
Hazardous materials workers who have quietly modified their units
story_hooks: A series of corporate equipment failures across competing firms all show signs of selective polymer dissolution. No ballistic evidence, no witnesses. Someone with an EDS-2 and an industrial license is running a quiet sabotage campaign.
A player is approached by a Zheng-Dao Bioelectric liaison who offers a significant payout to recover a specific EDS-2 unit — serial number provided. They won't say why that specific unit matters.
The players need to get through a door sealed with military-grade polymer adhesive. Someone mentions they know where to acquire a licensed decontamination sprayer.

A victim is found with dissolution injuries inconsistent with any known acid or solvent — the pattern suggests an ionized aerosol. The only legal holders of EDS-2 units in this district are three licensed industrial workers, all of whom have airtight alibis.
